subject: Architecture
title: The Rana Plaza Factory Collapse
description: One-minute skill: The Rana Plaza Factory Collapse.

hook.text: In 2013, a garment factory in Bangladesh collapsed, killing 1,134 workers — the deadliest structural failure in history.

buildup.text: Rana Plaza was an eight-story commercial building with three illegally added floors housing garment factories.

discovery.text: Large cracks appeared the day before. An engineer condemned the building. The owner ordered workers back inside.

twist.text: The factories supplied major Western fashion brands. Global consumers were unknowingly connected to the tragedy.

climax.text: The disaster sparked the global Fashion Revolution movement — 'Who made my clothes?' became a rallying cry.

punchline.text: 1,134 people died making clothes. The world asked who paid.

quiz.question: What movement did the Rana Plaza collapse inspire?
options: The Fair Trade certification for clothing
